findings.evidence: TauCeti/RingTheory/Semisimple/Multiplicity.lean: `variable {k A S : Type*} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] ...` `[FiniteDimensional k S]`, and `finrank_linearMap_eq_natCard_of_linearEquiv_pi (e : M ≃ₗ[A] ∀ i, N i)` with `[Finite ι]`.
findings.fix: Qualify the sentence: over an algebraically closed `k` and for a finite decomposition into simple modules, `finrank k (S →ₗ[k[N]] M)` counts the factors isomorphic to `S`; the transport results below use only the dimension, not that identification.
findings.issue: Module docstring: "the choice-free description that TauCeti/RingTheory/Semisimple/Multiplicity.lean proves counts the factors isomorphic to `S` in any decomposition of `M`" — that file proves the count only for `[IsAlgClosed k] [FiniteDimensional k S]` and a given *finite* decomposition. The implementation note at L86-89 says the opposite ("does need a splitting field"), so the docstring contradicts itself and overstates the imported result.

findings.evidence: L403-404: `theorem finrank_hom_pos [FiniteDimensional k V] {σ : Subrepresentation (ρ.comp N.subtype)} (hσ : σ ≠ ⊥)`.
findings.fix: Reword to "A nonzero `N`-subrepresentation has positive multiplicity", matching the companion `nontrivial_hom_of_ne_bot` docstring at L375.
findings.issue: `finrank_hom_pos` is documented as "A nonzero constituent has positive multiplicity", but its hypothesis is `σ ≠ ⊥`, not `IsAtom σ`; everywhere else in the file "constituent" means an atom (e.g. L365, L411).

summary: Twenty docstring cross-references name the new declarations as `TauCeti.Representation.X`, but this file declares them into the root `Representation` namespace, so every one of those links is dangling. The module docstring also states unconditionally that `RingTheory/Semisimple/Multiplicity.lean` proves the hom-space dimension counts isomorphic factors, omitting the `[IsAlgClosed k]`/finite-decomposition hypotheses and contradicting the file's own implementation note.
